# A function literal handed to a list method holds a ternary or a match, in a
# test body and in a prop: NoListLambdas makes the call a loop calling the
# literal in place, and NoTernary now lifts what that literal's body holds,
# which it reached as the call's callee and never visited -- every Go target
# panicked with "ir.Ternary reached Go codegen".

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

func short(name string) string {
    return match name {
        "north" => "N"
        "south" => "S"
        else => "?"
    }
}

component compass ui.node {
    var headings = ["north", "south", "up"]
    ui.text #label(value=headings.map(func(h string) => short(h)).format(","))
    ui.text #flags(value=headings.map(func(h string) => h == "up" ? "^" : "-").format(""))
}

func testALiteralInAPropLiftsItsBranches(t test.Test, c compass) {
    t.assert(c.label.value == "N,S,?")
    t.assert(c.flags.value == "--^")
}

func testALiteralInATestLiftsItsBranches(t test.Test, c compass) {
    var marks = c.headings.map(func(h string) => h == "north" ? "y" : "n").format("")
    t.assert(marks == "ynn")
    t.assert(c.headings.map(func(h string) => short(h)).format("") == "NS?")
}
